\section{Layered Architecture Model}
\label{sec:layered-architecture}

\subsection{Overview}
% [Member F] Describe the four-layer model at a high level.

The platform is organised into four horizontal layers
(\Cref{fig:layered-arch}), each with a well-defined responsibility and a
stable interface to the layer above.
Layers communicate only with adjacent layers; cross-layer calls are forbidden.

\begin{figure}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  font=\small,
  layer/.style={draw, rounded corners=3pt, minimum width=12cm,
                minimum height=1.1cm, align=center, inner sep=6pt},
  every node/.append style={font=\small}
]
  \node[layer, fill=blue!15]  (l4) {\textbf{Layer 4 -- Serving \& Monitoring}\\
    REST/gRPC endpoints \textbullet{} A/B routing \textbullet{} drift alerts};
  \node[layer, fill=green!15, below=4mm of l4] (l3) {\textbf{Layer 3 -- Model Registry \& Governance}\\
    Versioning \textbullet{} stage promotion \textbullet{} lineage};
  \node[layer, fill=yellow!20, below=4mm of l3] (l2) {\textbf{Layer 2 -- Training \& Experimentation}\\
    Pipeline orchestration \textbullet{} experiment tracking \textbullet{} evaluation};
  \node[layer, fill=orange!15, below=4mm of l2] (l1) {\textbf{Layer 1 -- Data \& Feature Engineering}\\
    Ingestion \textbullet{} validation \textbullet{} feature store};
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{The four-layer MLOps architecture.}
\label{fig:layered-arch}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Layer 1 -- Data and Feature Engineering}
% [Member F] Describe responsibilities, components, and interfaces of Layer 1.

\textbf{Responsibility.} Acquire raw data, validate its quality, compute
features, and make them available to Layer 2 (training) and Layer 4 (serving)
through the feature store API.

\textbf{Key components.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Ingestion connectors} -- pull from databases, event streams, and
        object storage.
  \item \emph{Validation step} -- schema and statistical checks; bad batches
        are quarantined, not silently dropped.
  \item \emph{Feature store} -- online store (low-latency reads for serving)
        and offline store (large-scale reads for training).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Layer 2 -- Training and Experimentation}
% [Member F] Describe responsibilities, components, and interfaces of Layer 2.

\textbf{Responsibility.} Train, evaluate, and select models using features
from Layer 1; push approved artefacts to Layer 3.

\textbf{Key components.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Pipeline orchestrator} -- directed acyclic graph (DAG) of
        preprocessing, training, and evaluation steps.
  \item \emph{Experiment tracker} -- records runs, parameters, and metrics.
  \item \emph{Evaluation gate} -- automatically compares a candidate model
        against the current champion; promotes only if it wins on the agreed
        metrics.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Layer 3 -- Model Registry and Governance}
% [Member F] Describe responsibilities, components, and interfaces of Layer 3.

\textbf{Responsibility.} Store and version model artefacts; govern their
lifecycle from \textit{staging} through \textit{production} to
\textit{archived}; expose a stable API to Layer 4.

\textbf{Key components.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Artefact store} -- binary storage for serialised models.
  \item \emph{Metadata store} -- lineage graph linking each model version to
        its training run, dataset version, and code commit.
  \item \emph{Approval workflow} -- human or automated sign-off before a model
        enters production.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Layer 4 -- Serving and Monitoring}
% [Member F] Describe responsibilities, components, and interfaces of Layer 4.

\textbf{Responsibility.} Serve model predictions with low latency; detect
degradation and trigger retraining events back to Layer 2.

\textbf{Key components.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Inference server} -- loads model artefacts from Layer 3; handles
        batching and hardware acceleration.
  \item \emph{Traffic router} -- supports canary releases and A/B experiments.
  \item \emph{Monitor} -- tracks data drift, prediction distribution, and
        business KPIs; publishes events when thresholds are breached.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Inter-Layer Contracts}
% [Member F] Summarise the APIs / event contracts between layers.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\caption{Inter-layer contracts.}
\label{tab:contracts}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}llX@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{From} & \textbf{To} & \textbf{Contract} \\
\midrule
L1 & L2 & Feature store offline read API (point-in-time query). \\
L1 & L4 & Feature store online read API (key--value lookup, <5\,ms p99). \\
L2 & L3 & Model push API (artefact + metadata JSON payload). \\
L3 & L4 & Model pull API (version tag or \texttt{latest-production} alias). \\
L4 & L2 & Drift event (message queue; schema versioned). \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}
